pages.text:
A big firebox: a hollow box that burns fuel into heat, enough to run the biggest Steam Boiler Array.
# Building
- A box 3 to 7 by 3 to 7 across (it needn't be square) and 3 to 7 tall, hollow inside.
- Its twelve edges are Firebox Array Casings. Walls, floor and roof are casings or Pressure Glass: through a window you can see the fire.
- One Firebox Array Controller sits in a side wall (not on an edge), facing out. Right-click it to open its GUI, or wrench it to check the build.
- It is lined with firebrick inside.

# Heat
The bigger it is, walls and inside, the more it makes: the largest, a 7×7×7, makes 50,400 HU/t, and a smaller one its share by volume (a 3×3×3 makes 3,967 HU/t). Its heat buffer grows with its size too.
- Solid fuels (coal, charcoal, coal blocks) give what they give in a Firebox (64,000 HU a coal) and burn at 1,100°C.
- Coal Coke (or Petroleum Coke) gives 1.5× a coal's heat (a Coal Coke Block 1.5× a coal block's) and burns at 1,300°C.
- Liquid and gas fuels give what they give in a Fuel Burner (Naphtha 400 HU per mB) at their own temperature (Hydrogen 1,400°C).
It finishes the item it started, then takes its tank's fuel before the next item. It pauses while it's as hot as its fuel burns, so no fuel is wasted.
# Oxy-fuel
Feed it oxygen through an Oxygen port: 300°C hotter (up to 1,600°C) and 25% more heat from each fuel, for about 3 mB of oxygen per 1,000 HU.

# Ports
A new array has none: set them on any casing (or the controller) with the Wrench in Port mode.
- Input: solid fuel, and liquid or gas fuel (a held bucket also fills it through the controller).
- Oxygen: oxygen for oxy-fuel.
- Heat: heat out. A Heat port pushes as fast as the array burns into whatever touches it, such as a Steam Boiler Array's heat port, or into Thermodynamic Conduits.
A Gas Output port (named Flue Gas) gives off Carbon Dioxide while it burns carbon fuels: see Carbon Capture.
